newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids lower, trade slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids lower, trade slow.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat bids were mostly lower on Monday in quiet conditions with selling interest largely restricted to producers with wheat coming out of a government loan program at the end of this month.
Dealers said some sales were close to being finalized but other producers in North Dakota and Montana were holding out, hoping the market may soon get back above $4.00 a bushel.
July MGE spring wheat futures closed off 1/4 cent at $3.90-1/2 a bushel.
They noted spring wheat plantings and emergence in USDA's weekly crop progress report was much as expected.
USDA reported that 95 percent of spring wheat had been planted and 70 percent emerged, little changed from the respective five-year averages of 92 and 77 percent.
